title: About me
intro: I make websites from the draft to going live, from the layout to the code. In the videos, who I am and what I build; in the cards, what I deliver and how we work together.

pessoal.title: Who I am
pessoal.srText: A roughly 26-second animation in neutral tones, with color photos and a soundtrack, styled like a video game. It opens and closes on João Carmassi's JC monogram. A "press start" screen opens on the name João Vitor Carmassi, and his card passes through the letters. The character select shows his photo card with the class "front-end developer" and the origin "são paulo, 2004". A pin on an aerial photo of Pedra do Baú marks his base in São Bento do Sapucaí, SP; the camera pulls back to a globe and routes fly out of it: "from the mountains to the world", "100% remote". Speech bubbles saying "olá", "hello" and "hola" show his languages: Portuguese native, English C1 and Spanish B2. In the inventory, six cubes hold hiking, motorcycle trips, music, games, movies and, equipped, code. It ends on "progress saved", the signature "joão." and github.com/joao-carmassi.

profissional.title: What I build
profissional.srText: A roughly 26-second animation in neutral tones, with color photos and a soundtrack. It opens and closes on João Carmassi's JC monogram. A hand-drawn sketch turns into a real website, reading "from sketch to live". A TypeScript component types itself out and the stack's icons appear: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind, Astro, GSAP, React Query, Zustand and Git. The camera flies through four kinds of project, shown with the real sites: business websites (Refúgio da Pedra, Dr. Jean Almeida), e-commerce (Loja do VRF), interactive maps (São Bento tourist map) and SaaS and dashboards (Quotation Factory, Higgx). Then a GSAP easing curve draws and a Prisma UI button is clicked, and under "SEO from day one" a search result climbs to first place while four Lighthouse scores fill to 100. It ends on João Carmassi, front-end developer, and "tell me about your project".
